events.summary: Speaker A reported the board's decision that the remote must be television only, reversing the universal remote idea.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: it needs to be television only

events.summary: Speaker A said the remote must include the company colours, red and black, and the slogan we put fashion in electronics.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: it needs to have the company colours included in it

events.summary: Speaker A decided not to include teletext in the design, as the board asked.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: so we don't wanna include that um in this particular design

events.summary: Speaker B reported from a preliminary study that too much metal can cause interference, false signals and a risk of the remote catching fire.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: too much metal in remote design could potentially cause interference with the ability of the remote to send commands

events.summary: Speaker B proposed primarily plastic construction, because of the interference and lawsuit risk from metal.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Therefore I suggest primarily plastic construction

events.summary: Speaker B proposed solar power with an alkaline battery backup as the energy source.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: maybe we could do something with solar power with an alkaline battery backup

events.summary: Speaker B said the remote should have a range of probably two hundred feet, with PAL and NTSC compatibility.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: probably a two hundred foot range

events.summary: Speaker B proposed infrared as the sender, because it is the industry standard.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I'm thinking infrared 'cause it is the industry standard

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a high grade recycled plastic for the user interface, since metal is out.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I was thinking maybe a high grade recycled plastic

events.summary: Speaker B reported that a laptop-style plastic finish is perfectly possible to make.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: the plastic they have on your laptop there is something that's perfectly possible for us to do

events.summary: Speaker C reported that complicated remotes have many functions, but most users do not use most of them because they do not know how.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: they won't use most of the functions because they don't know how to use them

events.summary: Speaker C proposed giving a complicated device's functionality with a simple formatted display, to revolutionise the remote.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: attain the functionality of a complicated device but use a simple formatted display

events.summary: Speaker D reported from a usability test of 100 people that most use only channel, on and off and volume, so the primary uses are basic.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: the primary uses are really really basic

events.summary: Speaker D reported that fifty percent of people say losing the remote is the worst thing about a remote.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: fifty percent of our people, their the worst thing about a remote is how often they lose it

events.summary: Speaker D reported that the younger demographics are all really interested in voice recognition options.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: the younger demographics are all really interested in voice recognition options

events.summary: Speaker A said the stats show that seventy five percent of people under thirty five thought about voice control.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: seventy five percent of people under thirty five wanted, thought about voice control

events.summary: Speaker A proposed looking into the younger demographic as the target market.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: maybe this we should look into this younger demographic

events.summary: Speaker A proposed voice operation for the basic controls, if it is doable, such as saying volume up.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: this voice operation thing is I think is a good idea

events.summary: Speaker B proposed combining the locator device with voice recognition, so a spoken locate command makes the remote beep.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I think it would be possible to uh combine the locator device and the voice recognition technology

events.summary: Speaker A objected that you cannot speak into the lost remote, because a remote hidden under the couch cannot pick up a voice from far away.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: you couldn't speak into the remote that you're trying to find

events.summary: Speaker A proposed making the small paging chip voice activated too, to solve the lost remote problem.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: maybe that could be voice activated too

events.summary: Speaker C proposed a sticky pad on top of the television, that the user speaks into to find the remote.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: A little sticky pad to stick on top of your uh television

events.summary: Speaker A said they like the voice recognition for the paging system, and will use it for the remote's paging function.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I like that, I like that, the voice recognition for the paging system

events.summary: Speaker C proposed keeping the remote simple with traditional buttons, and putting the complicated things into voice control, to sell to both younger and older markets.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we might be able to handle the simplicity of a remote control and kind of put the more complicated things into a voice control

events.summary: Speaker C reported that touch screens are technically possible and cost almost as little as buttons.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: they seem to be uh you know almost as cheap as a button method at this point

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a primary touch screen with four or five basic functions and menus for the complicated settings.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: your primary screen just be these you know four or five basic functions

events.summary: Speaker B objected that adding so much technology may break the twelve fifty Euro goal, because the microchip is the most expensive part.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: The microchip is probably the most expensive part of the the whole mechanism

events.summary: Speaker A decided to focus on the young demographic group, with bells and whistles available to anyone who wants them.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we're gonna just basically focus on this young demographic group, aim it at them

events.summary: Speaker C said the casing can stay fixed while the face plates are interchangeable, as on a mobile phone.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: We could have the casing, the the face plates

events.summary: Speaker B objected that including three or four face plates in the package will drive the cost up, and no market test has been done.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: say we're including three or four face plates, it's gonna drive the cost up

events.summary: Speaker B objected that face plates sound like a gimmick that would not go anywhere.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Off the top of my head it sounds kind of like a gimmick that wouldn't really go anywhere

events.summary: Speaker D said a face plate on a phone is visible when out and about, but a TV remote mostly sits at home.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: a face plate on a phone is you have it out and around

events.summary: Speaker C answered that most people keep the TV in the living room where guests can see it, so face plates can still be seen.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: most people have their televisions in the living room

events.summary: Speaker A decided to postpone the face plate question until the costs are worked out.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we can we can discuss that one further when we think about um whether th when we do costs

events.summary: Speaker A pointed out that a touch screen means users must recharge the remote, which may also help stop it being lost.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: if we have a touch screen people are going to have to recharge their remote controls

events.summary: Speaker A decided on a plastic casing, which is easy on cost, with high quality recycled plastic as Speaker B recommended.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: let's go for a plastic built or uh b plastic cased 'cause tha tha that's easy on the cost

events.summary: Speaker A provisionally decided on a touch screen with several submenus, with the channel and on and off switch on the touch screen.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: let's provisionally let's go for a touch screen one with several submenus

events.summary: Speaker A objected that nobody will buy a remote they have to plug in, so a new battery technology is needed.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I can't see anybody buying a lap a remote control that they have to plug in

events.summary: Speaker A decided on a touch screen remote with cutting edge battery technology, and said the team will look into it.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: with some kind of cutting edge battery technology

events.summary: Speaker A proposed making the channel and volume buttons large and easy to reach, with other functions in menus.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: make them large and easy to get at

events.summary: Speaker A proposed falling back to a well presented simple plastic remote if the new battery technology is not possible.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: if not we can always default to just doing a a well presented plastic simple

events.summary: Speaker A decided the voice recognition option will cover the simple functions, such as on and off, channels and volume.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: with this voice recognition option as well um just as for the simple functions

events.summary: Speaker A proposed a simple paging button that sends an infrared signal to make the remote beep, even without voice recognition.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: just some kind of simple button that's just a I guess another infrared signal to the remote control

events.summary: Speaker B asked whether users could input different skins for the touch screen interface.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: do we wanna look into the possibility of people being able to input different types of skins

events.summary: Speaker A objected that skins need a way to download or import, which is too much ports and cords for this product, so it is out of range for now.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: you'd need to have some way for people to download or import skins into the remote control

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a nice black and red interface on the touch screen to carry the company colours.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: we just need to come up with a nice black and red interface on the touch screen

events.summary: Speaker D proposed showing the slogan briefly each time the remote turns on, rather than engraving it on the back.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Comes on every time you turn it on and then that's it

events.summary: Speaker B objected that users do not want the remote to boot up with flashing things, they want it on and ready.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: People aren't gonna want their remote to boot up and to see flashing things come on

events.summary: Speaker C proposed that touching the screen wakes the remote, and it goes into a sleep mode, which saves battery.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: all you have to do is touch the screen and it automatically goes on

events.summary: Speaker A decided to put the logo on the boot up screen.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I like the idea of um putting the logo in the boot up screen
